records.title: Interposed signed editorial explanation of the opening invocations
records.arabic: لما كان هذا الكتاب مشتملاً على أهم المطالب الدينية وأعظم المقاصد اليقينية، بدأ رحمه الله بالبسملة اقتداءً بقوله عليه السلام: «كل أمر ذي بال لا يبدأ فيه ...» وإشارة إلى أن مثل هذا الأمر لا يتم إلا بالاستعانة به تعالى وحمده. وهذه البسملة للشارح، وبسملة المصنف هكذا: «بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم وبه نستعين في التتميم». وحذفناها استغناءً عنها. ⟦تلي ذلك جملة مطبوعة غير محرَّرة الضبط هنا، في بيان موضع البسملة في القسم الأول والإشارة إلى أهمية هذا القسم⟧. الفقير إليه فرج الله زكي الكردستاني المرواني الأزهري.
records.english: Because this book embraces the most important religious questions and the weightiest objects of certainty, the commentator—may God have mercy upon him—began with the invocation “In the name of God,” in imitation of the Prophetic saying about every matter of consequence that does not begin with it. He thereby indicates that a task of this kind is accomplished only by seeking God's help and praising Him. This invocation belongs to the commentator. The author of the underlying work begins: “In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate; in Him we seek help in completing [the work].” We omitted that invocation because the one already given suffices. [The following printed remarks on where the original author's wording appears, and the significance of the placement, are not secure enough to translate literally from the present scan.] [Signed:] The one in need of Him, Faraj Allāh Zakī al-Kurdistānī al-Marwānī al-Azharī.
records.attribution: Signed in print by Faraj Allāh Zakī al-Kurdistānī al-Marwānī al-Azharī
records.proof_note: Distinct middle-ruled register on printed I:2. Earlier corpus had only Sanandajī upper invocation and Wasīm lower preface. The final printed prose is partially illegible/uncertain; do not count as full literal page.

provenance.method: direct image inspection, uncertain endings retained

records.title: Sanandajī's invocation
records.arabic: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم. نحمد من هدانا إلى طريق الإسلام، حمداً يوافي نعمه؛ ونشكر الذي وفقنا على تهذيب الكلام وتقريب المرام، شكراً يكافئ مزيده؛ ونصلي صلاة دائمة ما دامت آثار العقائد الإسلامية باقية على صفحات الأيام، على سيدنا ونبينا محمد الذي بعثه إلى كافة الأنام واصطفاه لقمع الضلالة ورفع لواء الهدى، ⟦و... مقام الشفاعة يوم الجزا⟧، وعلى آله البررة الأنقياء.
records.english: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. We praise Him who guided us to the path of Islam, with a praise commensurate with His blessings; and thank Him who granted us success in refining theological discourse and bringing its aims within reach, with gratitude answering His increase in bounty. We invoke enduring blessings, for as long as the traces of Islamic belief remain upon the pages of the days, upon our master and Prophet Muḥammad, whom He sent to all humankind and chose to suppress misguidance and raise the banner of guidance, [followed by an ornamentally phrased invocation concerning intercession on the Day of Recompense whose exact wording requires further checking], and upon his noble, pure family. [The invocation continues at I:3.]
records.proof_note: Direct rereading of printed I:2 upper register. One ornate phrase remains bracketed; not a complete diplomatic proof.
records.provenance: source reread + inherited previous English + explanatory restatement; not certified

records.title: Distinct secondary invocation, linked to Wasīm I:3
records.arabic: بسم الله الرحمن الرحيم. الحمد لله الذي هدانا لدين الإسلام، ووفقنا على تحرير المقاصد الدينية وتهذيب الكلام، والصلاة والسلام على سيدنا ومقتدانا محمد خير الأنام وآله وعترته
records.english: In the name of God, the All-Merciful, the Compassionate. Praise belongs to God, who guided us to the religion of Islam and granted us success in elucidating religious aims and refining theological discourse. Blessings and peace upon our master and exemplar Muḥammad, the best of humankind, and upon his family and kin— [continues at I:3].
records.proof_note: Printed bottom register, self-identified in I:3; matched against earlier source-registered Wasīm preface, not inferred attribution from font or placement.
records.provenance: earlier self-identified Wasim preface translation; this stage only bibliographical attribution audit

records.title: Sanandajī explains his undertaking
records.arabic: وأصحابه الكرام الأصفياء * وبعد * فيقول العبد الفقير إلى ألطاف ربه الغني * عبد القادر ابن الشيخ محمد سعيد ⟦بقية النسبة غير محررة⟧ * لما كان قسم التهذيب من الكلام * الذي صنفه قدوة الأنام * العلامة الثاني * السعد التفتازاني * ⟦كلام غير منقول هنا⟧ * مع رشاقته ووجازته * مشتملاً على غرر أفكار ⟦…⟧ * إلى أن أشار إليّ من لا يسعني مخالفته * ولا يمكنني إلا موافقته * أن أشرحه شرحاً وافياً ⟦…⟧
records.arabic_anchors: «فيقول العبد الفقير إلى ألطاف ربه» · «عبد القادر» · «قسم التهذيب من الكلام» · «العلامة الثاني السعد التفتازاني».
records.english: ...and his noble, pure companions. Thereafter, the servant in need of the gracious favours of his Lord, the One free of need—ʿAbd al-Qādir, son of Shaykh Muḥammad Saʿīd [the remainder of the printed designation is not transcribed]—says: The theological division of the Tahdhīb, composed by the renowned scholar Saʿd al-Taftāzānī, despite its elegance and concision, comprises choice ideas [printed intervening language not transcribed here]. Then someone whose request I could not disobey, and with whom I could only agree, indicated that I should give it an ample commentary [the subsequent printed continuation is not yet transcribed].
records.proof_note: Stage 83: bounded transcription from original combined-PDF physical p.16 (printed I:3), upper register. First-pass reread of selected printed wording only, no claim of exact full-page or all-register translation. The personal designation, the ornate intervening prose and page-ending are open.
records.provenance: source reread + inherited previous English + explanatory restatement; not certified
records.stage81_legacy_english_overview: Sanandajī identifies himself as ʿAbd al-Qādir, a servant dependent upon God's favour, and describes the kalām section of Taftāzānī's *Tahdhīb* as unusually concise, carefully ordered and rich in subtle points. Although pressed by circumstances, he was urged by a person whose request he could not disregard to explain this difficult text. He therefore undertook a commentary intended to clarify its expressions and recover its intended senses. The sentence continues on I:4.
records.source_page_verification: Printed I:3, physical combined PDF p.16

records.title: Wasīm names himself and describes the commentary's origin
records.arabic: وكان المحصلون المترددون إلى والدنا الماجد راغبين في تحصيله عنده، ومنهم الأخ الأكبر الماهر الشيخ عبد القادر، وكان في أثناء تحصيله يراجع شرح المقاصد ويأخذ منه معاني دقيقة يكتبها حواشي على هذا المتن المتين بلفظ موجز متين، وبعد إتمام تحصيله جعلها شرحاً له.
records.arabic_anchors: «محمد الوسيم ابن المرحوم الشيخ محمد سعيد» · «ومنهم الأخ الأكبر الماهر الشيخ عبد القادر» · «يراجع شرح المقاصد».
records.english: The students who frequented our eminent father were eager to study it with him. Among them was my accomplished elder brother, Shaykh ʿAbd al-Qādir. While studying it, he would consult Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid and take from it subtle meanings, which he wrote as marginal annotations upon this substantial text in concise, precise language. When he had finished his study, he made those notes into a commentary on it.
records.proof_note: Stage 83: one contiguous bounded passage reread directly against the lower printed register on I:3 (physical PDF p.16). The preceding and following sentences are still omitted from this unit; this is not the full Wasīm preface.
records.provenance: earlier self-identified Wasim preface translation; this stage only bibliographical attribution audit
records.stage81_legacy_english_overview: In the lower stream, Muḥammad al-Wasīm explicitly names himself. He explains that students studying Taftāzānī with their father included his elder brother ʿAbd al-Qādir. During that study, ʿAbd al-Qādir consulted *Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid*, recording subtle explanations in brief marginal notes; he later made those into a continuous commentary. The shared family and teaching setting explains why the page must preserve **two different narrating voices**.
records.source_page_verification: Printed I:3, physical combined PDF p.16

records.title: Sanandajī's purpose and self-assessment
records.arabic: ⟦ابتداء الصفحة غير منقول هنا⟧ * خالياً عن شوائب الخلل والنقصان * عالياً أن تطرق إليه قلم النسخ والبطلان * ⟦كلام غير منقول هنا⟧ * وإن رده المتعصبون فسيقبله المنصفون * وإن كنت في ريب من المذكور فانظر ثم ارجع البصر هل ترى من فطور ⟦…⟧
records.arabic_anchors: «معانيه وتوضيح عباراته» · «فجاء بحمد الله ذلك شرحاً» · «خالياً عن شوائب الخلل والنقصان» · «فانظر ثم ارجع البصر هل ترى من فطور».
records.english: [The preceding printed description is not transcribed here.] [The author presents the commentary as] free from the admixture of defect and deficiency, beyond the pen of cancellation and annulment. [Intervening words are omitted.] Even if partisans reject it, equitable judges will receive it. If you doubt what has been said, look—and then turn your gaze again: do you see any fissure? [The page-end attribution and verses still require checking.]
records.proof_note: Stage 83: bounded printed excerpts from I:4 upper register, physical PDF p.17. The self-praising rhetoric and scriptural allusion are those of the historical author, NOT a modern editorial evaluation. Not a diplomatic transcription of page I:4.
records.provenance: source reread + inherited previous English + explanatory restatement; not certified
records.stage81_legacy_english_overview: The commentary aims to elucidate obscure expressions, clarify intellectual difficulties, and make subtle points accessible. The writer expresses the hope that his labour will be free of significant defects, yet rhetorically invites inspection: ‘Return your gaze: do you see any fissures?’ His praise also acknowledges the teaching of his father and the circumstances that allowed the work to come into being. This is an **authorial rhetorical appeal**, not a modern editorial claim of textual perfection.
records.source_page_verification: Printed I:4, physical combined PDF p.17

records.title: Revisions, hardship and relocation
records.arabic: ⟦افتتاح الصفحة غير منقول هنا⟧ وإني طالما كنت شائقاً إلى أن أكتب على الشرح حواشي تبين مواضعه المشكلة وتحل مسائله المعضلة، لكن ⟦…⟧ فلم تزل الحوادث تتزايد ⟦…⟧
records.arabic_anchors: «الشرح مرة ثانية» · «جرح وتعديل» · «أكتب على الشرح حواشي» · «تموجت أمواج المحن والفتن».
records.english: [The beginning of the printed continuation is not transcribed here.] I had long wished to write marginalia upon the commentary, to make clear its difficult passages and resolve its perplexing questions. But ... events went on multiplying [the subsequent narrative, including migration and the family’s circumstances, remains to be transcribed literally].
records.proof_note: Stage 83: one bounded sentence of Wasīm’s I:4 autobiographical lower register, with additional locating phrase. No claim of complete lower-page translation; historical narrative retained in legacy summary.
records.provenance: earlier self-identified Wasim preface translation; this stage only bibliographical attribution audit
records.stage81_legacy_english_overview: Wasīm recounts that his elder brother revised the commentary, changing or clarifying some passages. He had long hoped to compose notes on the commentary, to resolve difficult locations and questions. Repeated events delayed him, and disturbances grew until his elder brother left his homeland. Wasīm's account includes the brother's reception in Sulaymāniyya and Wasīm's own grief at separation. It is autobiographical source material; **these historical particulars are not part of Sanandajī's original kalām argument**.
records.source_page_verification: Printed I:4, physical combined PDF p.17

records.title: The title *Taqrīb al-Marām*
records.arabic: ولما وفقت بعون الله للإتمام * سميته تقريب المرام * في شرح تهذيب الكلام * أسأل الله أن ينفع به كل ذي ⟦نعت غير متيقن⟧ * بحرمة سيدنا ومقتدانا محمد الهاشمي القرشي * صلى الله عليه وسلم وعلى آله كل غدا وعشي.
records.arabic_anchors: «سميته تقريب المرام في شرح تهذيب الكلام» · «محمد الهاشمي القرشي».
records.english: And when, by God’s help, I was enabled to bring it to completion, I called it Taqrīb al-Marām, a commentary on Tahdhīb al-Kalām. I ask God to make it beneficial to every [the printed epithet is not securely read], by the honour of our master and exemplar Muḥammad, the Hāshimī and Qurashī. May God bless him, and his family, morning and evening.
records.proof_note: Stage 83: near-continuous source reading of the small upper closing register on I:5 (physical PDF p.18); a rhyming epithet and some orthographic detail still require a second visual proof. The lower Wasīm text on the same page is a different voice.
records.provenance: source reread + inherited previous English + explanatory restatement; not certified
records.stage81_legacy_english_overview: Having composed the commentary, Sanandajī gives it the title *Taqrīb al-Marām fī Sharḥ Tahdhīb al-Kalām*—roughly ‘Bringing the Intended Aim Near: a Commentary on the Refinement of Theological Discourse.’ He closes with a prayer that it benefit its readers and a benediction upon Muḥammad the Hāshimī and Qurashī. The prayer, like the opening, is in rhymed prose.
records.source_page_verification: Printed I:5, physical combined PDF p.18

records.title: Wasīm closes his introduction
records.arabic: ⟦صدر النص غير منقول هنا⟧ وتم الفراغ في سنة ألف ومائتين وثلاثة وسبعين من الهجرة النبوية على صاحبها أزكى التحية.
records.arabic_anchors: «سنة ألف ومائتين وثلاثة وسبعين» · «النبوة».
records.english: [The preceding lower-register remarks are not transcribed here.] The completion occurred in 1273 AH, counted from the Prophetic Emigration—upon its bearer be the purest salutations. The exact antecedent of “completion” requires the whole closing statement and should not automatically be treated as the date of the Būlāq printing or of Sanandajī’s entire original commentary.
records.proof_note: Stage 83: selected closing date clause in Wasīm’s lower I:5, physical PDF p.18. Its historical referent cannot safely be decided from the extracted clause alone. The source scan must control the date and its surrounding syntax.
records.provenance: earlier self-identified Wasim preface translation; this stage only bibliographical attribution audit
records.stage81_legacy_english_overview: Wasīm's prefatory account concludes with its own reflection on the work's publication, the benefits and difficulties of the commentary, and a stated completion date of **1273 AH**. That date belongs to **his account of completing the prefatory/annotation work**, not automatically to the Būlāq edition or to every portion of the sharḥ. Its exact referent should be established from the entire closing sentence during independent checking.
records.source_page_verification: Printed I:5, physical combined PDF p.18

records.title: Can the chapter plan itself count as the beginning of kalām?
records.arabic: قال (هذا قسم الكلام من التهذيب) أقول لما ذكر من الديباجة أن هذا غاية تهذيب الكلام في تحرير المنطق والكلام علم أن كتابه قسمان: قسم في تحرير المنطق وقسم في تحرير الكلام، ثم لما قال الأول في المنطق كان الأوفق هنا أن يقول الثاني في الكلام، إلا أنه لما صرح بأولية ما في المنطق استغنى عن التصريح بثانوية ما في الكلام، فعدل إلى هذا تفنناً، فيكون الحاصل أن هذا هو القسم الآخر من الكلام المهذب الكائن في تحرير علم الكلام، فالظاهر أن إضافة القسم إلى الكلام إضافة الدال إلى المدلول.
records.arabic_anchors: «(قوله هذا قسم الكلام من التهذيب)» · «غاية تهذيب الكلام» · «في تحرير المنطق وتحرير الكلام» · «ألفاظ ... قسماً من العلم».
records.english: He said, “This is the kalām division of the Tahdhīb.” I say: since the preface mentioned that the work seeks the utmost refinement of discourse in treating logic and kalām, one knows that his book has two divisions: one devoted to the treatment of logic and one devoted to the treatment of kalām. When he had spoken of the first as concerning logic, the most fitting expression here would have been “the second, concerning kalām.” But having explicitly stated the priority of the logic section, he had no need to state explicitly that the kalām section came second. He varied his expression and used “this” instead. The result is that this is the other division of the refined discourse, the one concerned with the science of kalām. Accordingly, the relation of “division” to “kalām” is evidently the relation of the signifying expression to what it signifies. [The lower argument continues and is not exhausted by this excerpt.]
records.proof_note: Source-facing marginal reading; not every subordinate example individually translated.
records.provenance: source reread + inherited previous English + explanatory restatement; not certified
records.stage87_previous_english: The marginal writer examines what is implied by calling this the kalām division of a book which also concerns logic. One might take the wording to mean that the book is ‘refined’ in its entirety; another reading limits the title's effect to the matters explicitly treated under it. The gloss distinguishes a **textual division**, a **field of knowledge**, and the act of **refining a discourse** about that field. The point is relevant because the two sections need not have precisely the same objects, terminology, or demonstrative aim.
records.stage87_source_note: Visually read continuous opening stretch of the lower commentary, Būlāq I:6. This is a selected span, not the entire lower annotation. No identified author in the cropped span.
records.stage87_copytext: Būlāq 1318 AH, Vol. I printed p.6, original combined PDF physical p.19

records.title: Preliminary matters and subject-matter
records.arabic: ما يتوقف عليه الشروع في مسائل العلم من معرفة الحد والموضوع وغرضهما
records.arabic_anchors: «المقدمة» · «الحدّ والموضوع» · «مباحث العلم والنظر» · «التعريف».
records.english: That upon which embarking upon the problems of the science depends: knowing its definition, its subject, and their aims. [This is a selected clause near the end of the same lower printed block, not a separate authorial note.]
records.proof_note: Connected interpretative lower text, requires literal second pass.
records.provenance: source reread + inherited previous English + explanatory restatement; not certified
records.stage87_previous_english: The marginal argument also asks which preliminary matters are genuinely needed for the science. A definition of a discipline may address its name, subject, end and benefit; a preliminary discussion may also address the meaning of knowledge and the role of inquiry. Those questions are introduced as **instruments** for the ensuing theological investigation. The writer warns against treating every preliminary logical discussion as though it were already a doctrinal conclusion.
records.stage87_source_note: Selected lower-register clause near end of printed I:6; existing separate record is an editorial subdivision of a running lower passage; word preceding the clause and continuation are withheld.
records.stage87_copytext: Būlāq 1318 AH, Vol. I printed p.6, original combined PDF physical p.19

records.title: On the expression ‘section of kalām’
records.arabic: (قوله أي ما سيتلى عليك) يشير إلى أن (هذا) عبارة من الألفاظ من حيث دلالتها على المعاني. اه فرج الله زكي. (قوله المسمى بالتهذيب) أي في عرف المحصلين. اه منه.
records.arabic_anchors: «(قوله أي ما سيأتي عليك)» · «هذا إشارة من الألفاظ من حيث دلالتها على المعاني» · «(قوله المسمى بالتهذيب)».
records.english: On his words “that is, what will be recited to you”: he indicates that “this” belongs to expressions considered insofar as they signify meanings. [Signed:] Faraj Allāh Zakī. On “called al-Tahdhīb”: that is, by the usage of those who study the work. [By the same writer.] [A longer subsequent ruled discussion of the title remains untranslated here.]
records.proof_note: Short ruled annotation with an uncertain proper-name reading.
records.provenance: source reread + inherited previous English + explanatory restatement; not certified
records.stage87_previous_english: On the words “what will come before you,” the commentator points out how the demonstrative is attached to what follows in the written exposition. The title ‘Tahdhīb’ and the expression ‘the division of kalām’ are accordingly explained as designating a **part of a composed text**, not an independently existing scientific object. The gloss also discusses the phrasing and attribution of the title; a short name in the final line is not confidently legible.
records.stage87_source_note: Two directly legible entries at top of ruled middle register, I:6. Not attributed to Wasīm; the subsequent longer note is not covered.
records.stage87_copytext: Būlāq 1318 AH, Vol. I printed p.6, original combined PDF physical p.19

records.title: The intended portion of the book
records.arabic: (هذا) أي ما سيتلى عليك (قسم الكلام من) الكتاب المسمى (بالتهذيب وعلى الستة وقع التبويب) لأن ما ذكر فيه إما أن يجب تقدمه في علم الكلام وهو الباب الأول في المقدمة أولاً، وحينئذ إما أن يبحث فيه عما يختص بواحد من الأقسام.
records.arabic_anchors: «(هذا) أي ما سيأتي عليك (قسم الكلام من) الكتاب المسمى (بالتهذيب)» · «وقع التبويب» · «المقدمة أولاً».
records.english: “This”—that is, what is about to be set before you—“is the kalām division of” the book called “al-Tahdhīb; and the arrangement into six chapters has been made.” For what is mentioned therein must either precede [the discussion] in the science of kalām—this is Chapter One, the introduction—or else it treats something peculiar to one of the divisions. [The classification continues on the next printed page.]
records.proof_note: Stage 83: bounded first and third Arabic spans reread from I:6 upper register, physical PDF page 19. The exact intervening classification and separately ruled marginal streams still need transcription.
records.provenance: source reread + inherited previous English + explanatory restatement; not certified
records.stage81_legacy_english_overview: “This”—that is, the material about to be presented—is the **division on kalām** in the book called *al-Tahdhīb*. The reason the author has arranged it in chapters is that there are matters which ought to be introduced before the substantive questions of theology. They form the first chapter, a preliminary section; only once those conceptual preliminaries have been set out can the later questions be investigated. The work's division and naming are therefore not arbitrary ornaments but mark the progression of the inquiry.
records.source_page_verification: Printed I:6, physical combined PDF p.19
records.stage87_previous_arabic: (هذا) أي ما سيأتي عليك (قسم الكلام من) الكتاب المسمى (بالتهذيب) ⟦بقية الوصلة في التبويب غير منقولة⟧ لأن ما ذكر فيه إما أن يجب تقدمه في علم الكلام وهو الباب الأول في المقدمة أولاً ⟦…⟧
records.stage87_previous_english: “This,” meaning what is about to come before you, “is the kalām division” of the book called al-Tahdhīb. [The intervening description of its chapter arrangement has not yet been copied.] What is discussed in it either needs to precede the investigation of kalām; such material belongs in the first chapter, the introduction [the remaining division is not yet transcribed].
records.stage87_source_note: Direct reading of the three upper lines, physical PDF p.19; the join to I:7 is not a separate new work. A connective near the end remains a first-pass reading; recheck before full-page acceptance.
records.stage87_copytext: Būlāq 1318 AH, Vol. I printed p.6, original combined PDF physical p.19

records.title: What does ‘chapter’ denote?
records.arabic: ضرورة أن الظاهر من الأبواب هي الألفاظ أو النقوش
records.arabic_anchors: «في الباب الأول في المقدمة» · «الظاهر أن الأبواب هي الألفاظ أو النقوش» · «النظر أولاً».
records.english: For it is evident that what is meant by “chapters” is the expressions or the written inscriptions. [The surrounding lower argument about headings and the introduction remains to be transcribed.]
records.proof_note: Marginal source-facing explanation; some editorial connective phrasing used.
records.provenance: source reread + inherited previous English + explanatory restatement; not certified
records.stage87_previous_english: The lower writer observes that a ‘chapter’ can designate the **written headings or sections** of the treatise rather than a metaphysical part of the subject-matter. He is concerned to avoid a purely verbal inference from a heading to a division of reality. The introductory chapter is not the whole of kalām merely because it contains prerequisites of kalām; its function is to explain what the science is and how its arguments proceed.
records.stage87_source_note: One directly seen clause within the lower printed block. This is a selected quotation, not full lower-note translation.

records.title: What should come before the scientific questions?
records.arabic_anchors: «مباحث العلم والنظر» · «التصور والتصديق» · «المقدمة» · «ما يتوقف عليه الشروع في مسائل العلم».
records.english: The gloss asks whether the actual investigation of first principles should precede the definition of the science, or whether the introductory description is sufficient for a reader who has not yet learned the relevant principles. Some knowledge of **conception**, **assent**, and **valid reasoning** is indispensable before proof is possible. But it does not follow that every such preliminary must itself be independently proven at the beginning of the treatise. The author is explaining a pedagogical order, not claiming that the order of printed headings dictates the order of things in the world.
records.proof_note: Provisional connected gloss; word-exhaustive proof pending.

records.title: Sequence of the later chapters
records.arabic: ⟦الوصل من I:6⟧ وهو الباب الثاني في الأمور العامة، أو ما يختص بالممكن الذي لا يقوم بنفسه بل بغيره وهو الباب الثالث في الأعراض، أو بالممكن الذي يقوم بنفسه وهو الباب الرابع في الجواهر، وأما الواجب تعالى فإما باعتبار إرساله الرسل وبعثه الأنبياء وهو الباب السادس في السمعيات، أو لا باعتباره وهو الباب الخامس في الإلهيات. الباب الأول في المقدمة. منها ما يراد تقديمه في كل علم كمعرفة حده وموضوعه وغايته، ومنها ما صدروا به علم ⟦يتصل بـ I:8: الكلام خاصة⟧.
records.arabic_anchors: «الثلاثة في الوجود وهو الباب الثاني في الأمور العامة» · «الثالث في الأعراض» · «الرابع في الجواهر» · «الخامس ... بالواجب تعالى» · «السادس في السمعيات ... الباب الخامس في الإلهيات».
records.english: [Continuing the classification from I:6:] This is Chapter Two, on general matters; or [one treats] what pertains to a contingent thing which does not subsist by itself but in another—Chapter Three, on accidents; or what pertains to a contingent thing that subsists by itself—Chapter Four, on substances. As for the Exalted Necessary One, He may be considered with regard to His sending messengers and raising up prophets—Chapter Six, on matters known through transmitted revelation—or apart from that consideration—Chapter Five, on divine matters. Chapter One: Introduction. Of [the preliminary matters], some are to be presented in every science, such as knowledge of its definition, subject and purpose; others are matters with which they introduced the science of ... [continued on I:8: kalām in particular].
records.proof_note: Stage 83: a sustained transcription of the upper register on I:7, physical PDF p.20, excluding the uncertain initial connection. The page also has separately ruled and lower registers, neither fully proofed. The apparently nonsequential mention of sixth before fifth follows the printed argument and must not be silently reordered.
records.provenance: source reread + inherited previous English + explanatory restatement; not certified
records.stage81_legacy_english_overview: After the preliminary chapter, the subject is arranged in a progression: the **general matters of being**; matters concerning **accidents**; matters concerning **substances**; the **Necessary Existent**, or what pertains to God; and finally the **things known by transmission**, where the revealed reports and the mission of the Messenger are treated. The chapter headings have their own technical ordering, and the commentator explains how the labels for the wider theological divisions correspond to the actual sequence within the *Tahdhīb*.
records.source_page_verification: Printed I:7, physical combined PDF p.20
records.stage87_previous_arabic: ⟦ابتداء الوصلة من الصفحة السابقة غير منقول هنا⟧ وهو الباب الثاني في الأمور العامة، أو ما يختص بالممكن الذي لا يقوم بنفسه بل بغيره وهو الباب الثالث في الأعراض، أو بالممكن الذي يقوم بنفسه وهو الباب الرابع في الجواهر، وأما الواجب تعالى فإما باعتبار إرساله الرسل وبعثه الأنبياء وهو الباب السادس في السمعيات، أو لا باعتباره وهو الباب الخامس في الإلهيات. الباب الأول في المقدمة.
