records.title: “Taken with something” and “taken without a condition”
records.english: Quiddity taken on condition of something, as indicated by its contrast with the preceding case, is the meaning conceived not in isolation. If something accompanies it, that thing is considered included in it; the meaning thus becomes identical with the composite whole in the circumstance of their conjunction. Quiddity taken without a condition, by contrast, is likewise not considered in isolation, but if something accompanies it neither its inclusion nor its exclusion is stipulated. The meaning consequently remains indeterminate and capable of being predicated of the whole composite when the conjunction obtains. [The Arabic term for predicability is proposed from a parallel, not independently collated.]
records.arabic: والماهية المأخوذة بشرط شيء بقرينة تقابلها بما سبق ما يتصور معناها لا وحده بحيث لو قارنها شيء اعتبر داخلا فيها فيكون ذلك المعنى عين المجموع المركب حال المقارنة والمأخوذة لا بشرط شيء ما يتصور معناها لا وحده بحيث لو قارنها شيء لم يشترط دخوله فيها ولا عدم دخوله فيكون مبهما محتملا ⟦للمقولية⟧ على المجموع حال المقارنة
notes: The long marginal argument includes subtle changes between *predicated of the whole* and *a component of the whole*. English has been kept tied to those conceptual alternatives. Certain compressed words between the three definitions need a second line-level comparison.
records.prior_english_stage77: Quiddity *taken on condition of something* (*bi-sharṭ shayʾ*), understood in contrast to the preceding case, is conceived so that the accompanying qualification is **counted within it**; the original meaning is then treated as the composite whole in the circumstance of conjunction. By contrast, quiddity *taken without condition* (*lā bi-sharṭ*) is not conceived with the stipulation that the accompanying thing be included, nor with the stipulation that it be excluded. Its meaning remains **unspecified as regards inclusion**, capable of being predicated of the whole in which another qualification is present, and not defined as an intrinsically separate part of that whole. The distinction is a distinction in how the meaning is considered, not proof of additional externally existing constituents.
records.prior_arabic_anchors_stage77: «والماهية المأخوذة بشرط شيء بقرينة تقابلها بما سبق ما يتصور معناها لا وحده بحيث لو قارنها شيء اعتبر داخلا فيها» · «فيكون ذلك المعنى عين المجموع المركب حال المقارنة» · «والمأخوذة لا بشرط شيء ما يتصور معناها لا وحده» · «ولا عدم دخوله فيكون مبهما محتملا للقسمة على المجموع حال المقارنة».

uncertain_readings: The word after محتملا resembles للمقولية but has not been independently confirmed; marked ⟦...؟⟧ rather than passed off as a certified reading
The verb لا يشترط/لم يشترط needs precise consonantal check

critical_apparatus.prior_reading: لو قارنها شيء لا يشترط دخوله
critical_apparatus.current_reading: لو قارنها شيء لم يشترط دخوله

critical_apparatus.printed_reading: ink compressed at this locus; likely للمقولية
critical_apparatus.basis: Būlāq I:73 local image; exact quoted formulation in Taftāzānī, Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid, vol. I p.100: مبهما محتملا للمقولية; related Ibn Sīnā formulation. Parallel only, not independent Taqrīb witness.

records.title: Animal, human, and the genus/species illustration
records.english: Thus, when animal [animality] is considered in the first sense, it is a part of the composite—for example, the human being. Considered in the second sense, it constitutes a species, the human being, for example. Considered in the third, it becomes a genus predicable of the human being and of other, different realities that share animality. On this terminology, quiddity taken on condition of something—the one called the mixed [or conditioned] quiddity—is the composite of the quiddity and what accompanies it. It is therefore identical with the individuals, without the earlier objection necessarily following.
records.arabic: فالحيوان إذا اعتبر بالمعنى الأول يكون جزءا للمركب الذي هو الإنسان مثلا وإذا اعتبر بالمعنى الثاني يكون نوعا هو الإنسان مثلا وإذا اعتبر بالمعنى الثالث يكون جنسا مقولا على الإنسان وغيره من الحقائق المختلفة المشتركة في الحيوانية فعلى هذا الاصطلاح تكون الماهية المأخوذة بشرط شيء المسماة بالمخلوطة عبارة عن المركب من الماهية وما يقارنها فتكون عين الأفراد من غير لزوم ما سبق من الاعتراض
records.prior_english_stage77: For example, if “animal” is considered in the **first** sense, it is a part of the composite that is a human being. Considered in the **second** sense, it may be the species human [under the composite consideration]. Considered in the **third** sense, it is a **genus predicable of the human being and of others**, the different realities that share animality. On this usage, the quiddity taken under a restrictive condition may be a component of the composite, while what is taken without that condition can be a genus shared among individuals. Yet the conclusion must not be generalized to every logical combination without checking which meaning of “part,” “species” and “genus” is actually under discussion.
records.prior_arabic_anchors_stage77: «إذا اعتبر المعنى الأول يكون جزءا للمركب الذي هو الإنسان مثلا» · «وإذا اعتبر المعنى الثاني يكون نوعا هو الإنسان مثلا» · «وإذا اعتبر بالمعنى الثالث يكون جنسا مقولا على الإنسان وغيره» · «الحقائق المختلفة المشتركة في الحيوانية».
records.source_visual_check: original Vol I p.73 (combined physical PDF p.86); same-editor image comparison; uncertain words remain
uncertain_readings: The phrase المسماة بالمخلوطة is printed with compressed dots; its precise vocalization and editorial punctuation require confirmation

records.title: Matter, form, and why the alleged genus is not automatically a real part
records.english: Nor is it then necessary to appeal to the author's earlier statement that calling the species “what is taken on condition of something” is merely a latitude of expression, based on species, genus and differentia being one in the underlying thing. Even if that holds for quiddity in relation to the species beneath it, its relation to varieties and individuals still needs consideration. Reflect. Quiddity taken without condition—the unrestricted quiddity—remains indeterminate and open to predication. In that respect it is a genus or a common accident; it is not, considered simply under that concept, identical with what it is truly said of or a part of that thing. Nevertheless, in respect of actual denotation, it cannot but be either a constituent or identical with its instances. As noted above, the concepts exclude one another under the distinct descriptions, while their ranges of predication stand in relations of greater and lesser generality.
records.arabic: ومن غير احتياج إلى ما سبق من المصنف من أن جعل النوع عبارة عن المأخوذة بشرط شيء مسامحة مبنية على كون النوع والجنس والفصل واحدا بالذات فإنه إذا تم في الماهية بالنسبة إلى الأنواع دونها بالنسبة إلى الأصناف والأشخاص فتأمل وتكون الماهية لا بشرط شيء أعني المطلقة مبهمة محتملة ⟦للمقولية؟⟧ ومن هذه الحيثية تكون جنسا أو عرضا عاما لا عينا لما صدقها ولا جزءا منها وإن كانت من حيث الصدق لا تخلو من أن تكون جزءا أو عينا لها كما سبق أنها من حيث المفهوم متنافية ومن حيث الصدق أعم منها
notes: The compressed phrase naming the “mixed” or “conditioned” quiddity requires visual proof before its Arabic wording is fixed; the above is a working conceptual rendering, not a silently reconstructed quotation.
records.prior_english_stage77: If quiddity is taken with or apart from conditions in the different senses just described, the result can be described as the composite of a meaning with its accompanying qualifications, or as the individual things of which that meaning is said. The familiar objection—that the compound would then need a second constituent in addition to its asserted quiddity—does not follow automatically. Nor is there always a need to say, as the author previously did, that calling the species “the quiddity taken on condition of something” is merely a concession of usage. The logical status of the same meaning changes with the **level of comparison**: it may function as genus relative to what falls below it and as species relative to what falls above it, and when it is considered in relation to kinds, varieties and individual persons, the relations change accordingly. The commentator is distinguishing the conceptual function of these classifications rather than supposing that each name establishes an independent part outside the mind.
records.prior_arabic_anchors_stage77: «تكون الماهية المأخوذة بشرط لا شيء المسماة بالمخلوطة عبارة عن المركب من الماهية وما يقارنها» · «فتكون عين الأفراد من غير لزوم ما سبق من الاعتراض» · «ولا احتياج إلى ما سبق من المصنف من أن جعل النوع عبارة عن المأخوذ بشرط شيء مسامحة» · «لأن الماهية بالنسبة إلى الأنواع دونها بالنسبة إلى الأصناف والأشخاص».
records.source_visual_check: original Vol I p.73 (combined physical PDF p.86); same-editor image comparison; uncertain words remain

The phrase فإنه إذا تم في الماهية بالنسبة إلى الأنواع is syntactically compressed; English clause remains provisional

critical_apparatus.basis: Comparable technical usage in Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid I:100; Būlāq I:73 local glyphs remain congested. Do not silently emend.

records.title: Universal predication, qualification, and the wording of the *Maqāṣid*
records.english: It follows that treating the non-indeterminate [restricted] cases as divisions of this quiddity is legitimate only when one considers what the expressions apply to. Hence the author's statement in the Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid, referring to what has preceded, that the first is more general than the second means that it is more general with respect to denotation, not with respect to conceptual meaning. A quiddity considered without stipulating that something accompany it is a predicable genus only insofar as it is considered indeterminately. What matters is not a stipulation that the accompanying feature be inside it or outside it, but the possibility of considering it in the appropriate way. [The concluding phrase is elliptical and may continue conceptually on the next leaf.]
records.arabic: فظهر أن جعل غير المبهم من أقسام هذه الماهية إنما هو من حيث الصدق فمعنى قول المصنف في شرح المقاصد أن معنى ذلك على ما مر من كون الأول أعم من الثاني هو أنه كذلك بحسب الصدق لا المفهوم فالمأخوذة لا بشرط أن يكون معه شيء إنما يكون جنسا محمولا إذا كان معتبرا على سبيل الإبهام بحيث يكون فيها لا أن يعتبر المقارن له داخلا فيه وخارجا عنه فالمعتبر فيه هو صلاحية اعتباره
notes: outgoing I074.lower.01.
records.prior_english_stage77: Considered **as meanings**, some of these classifications stand in opposition; considered **in respect of predication**, one can be more general than another. The lower commentator accordingly questions the division that places an unrestricted meaning and its qualified instances within a single univocal taxonomy. A phrase in *Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid* that calls the first sense broader than the second should not be interpreted without specifying whether “broader” concerns the **concept** or the **things of which it is true**. Something counted as a genus in a predication may not, for that reason alone, be a real constituent of the external object. In particular, *not stipulating that something must accompany it* differs from stipulating that nothing accompanies it. The commentary continues into I:74 with a qualification about what may count as a genuine constituent.
records.prior_arabic_anchors_stage77: «من حيث المفهوم متنافية ومن حيث الصدق أعم منها» · «أن جعل غير المبهم من أقسام هذه الماهية» · «فمعنى قول المصنف في شرح المقاصد أن معنى ذلك على ما من كون الأول أعم من الثاني» · «لا بشرط أن يكون معه شيء إنما يكون جنسا محمولا».
records.source_visual_check: original Vol I p.73 (combined physical PDF p.86); same-editor image comparison; uncertain words remain
uncertain_readings: Last clause begins فالمأخوذة لا بشرط أن يكون معه شيء; syntactic scope of أن requires second proof
The closing sentence should be reconciled with the continuation of lower discussion on I:74

records.title: The end of the I:73 classification, and the danger of moving between senses
records.arabic_anchors: «واتحاده معا فلو اعتبر فيه التغاير فقط أو الاتحاد فقط كان الأول جزءا والثاني نوعا لا جنسا» · «وظاهر عبارة الشارح» · «لم يخف أنه استثناء من جميع ما سبق أن الماهية سواء على القول المتصور أو على اصطلاح الشيخ».
records.english: —[The relevant meaning admits] both difference and identity together. If only **difference** were considered it would be a **part**; if only **identity** were considered it would be a **species**, not a genus. The outward wording of the commentator must therefore be read with the different senses distinguished. His expression does not by itself provide an unambiguous textual decision between the classifications previously discussed. Further, the earlier division of quiddity—whether according to the familiar classification or the Chief Master's terminology—divides it **as considered**, not as though the divisions were independently existing external quiddities. In the actual case one must still ask how the considered meaning is related to a thing's unity and its individuating features.

records.title: What “no parts” means and why the simple cannot be a hidden composite
records.arabic_anchors: «(قوله لا جزء لها) أي في حد ذاتها» · «(قوله تقابلها) أشار به إلى أن البساطة والتركيب بهذا التفسير متنافيان» · «أن البساطة والتركيب بهذا التفسير متنافيان لا يصدقان على شيء» · «وقد يؤخذان متضايفين».
records.english: On “It has no part”: that is, **in its own definition or essence**. On the discussion of opposition: the expressions **simplicity** and **composition**, under one sense of the definitions given, are mutually exclusive and cannot both be true of one and the same thing in the same respect. Yet the terms can also be used **relationally**. A thing may be simple relative to one analysis and composite relative to another. One must therefore prevent an inference that assumes they are absolutely contradictory while employing them in a comparative sense.

records.title: Conceptual parts versus real constituents
records.arabic_anchors: «قد يوخذ البسيط بمعنى ما لا جزء له بالقياس إلى ما هو مركب منه» · «وقد يؤخذ المركب بمعنى جزء المركب والمركب بمعنى الكل» · «وبهذا التقدير لا يمنع من صدقهما» · «(قوله لأن الواحد مبدأ المتعدد الخ) أراد من الواحد والمتعدد».
records.english: The simple may be taken in a restricted sense as **what is not a part of the relevant kind**, or as what does not have a part relative to a proposed composite. The composite in turn can be described in terms of its own component and the whole into which that component enters. Under a comparative interpretation some predicates of simplicity and composition can apply without inconsistency, so one cannot argue from the bare words to a contradiction. On “For unity is the principle of multiplicity”: what matters is the distinction between **the one and the many in the order being considered**. It should not be inferred without proof that an unrestricted unity is a real, separate constituent in every enumerated collection. The marginal argument on I:75 continues this issue by examining the attempted regress from multiplicity to unity.
notes: I075.lower.01.

records.title: Real composition implies simplicity, without a regress of actual parts
records.arabic_anchors: «لا جزء لها كالنقطة» · «وأما كيفية تقابلها كالجسم» · «ولا يخفى وجود الماهية المركبة ويلزم منه وجود البسيطة» · «(ولا بد من الانتهاء إلى البسيطة)» · «لأن الواحد مبدأ المتعدد».
records.english: “It has no part, like a point.”
records.arabic: لا جزء لها كالنقطة
records.attribution: Taftazani embedded lemmas within Sanandaji commentary
notes: I072.upper.01, not I073: the entire intervening I:73 is printed marginal commentary.
records.stage86_prior_english_analytic_draft: —[A simple quiddity] has no parts, as in the case of a point; other examples of what stands opposed to it are treated according to the kind of composition meant, such as body. The existence of **composite quiddities** is not in dispute, and the existence of composites entails that there must also be **simple quiddities**. “There must be an end at something simple.” For unity is the principle of multiplicity: if every one were itself a multitude of parts, whether finite or infinite, and every supposed constituent were in turn divisible without terminus, the account of an actually existing composite would fail to provide the basic unities on which the composition depends. The point is not merely that the intellect can divide a concept, but that the analysis of an actual composite cannot proceed without end in the way alleged.
records.stage86_source_note: Short lemma on simple quiddity.
records.stage86_copytext: Būlāq 1318 AH, printed Volume I:74, physical combined PDF p.87
records.stage86_attribution_policy: Upper, ruled and lower voices retained separately; no unassigned note is attributed to Wasīm

records.title: Mutual dependence of the constituents of a real composite
records.arabic_anchors: «(واحتياج بعض الأجزاء إلى بعض في المركب الحقيقي ضروري)» · «إذ لو استغنى كل من الأجزاء عن الآخر لم يحصل منها».
records.english: “Some of the parts of a real composite must depend upon others.”
records.arabic: واحتياج بعض الأجزاء إلى بعض في المركب الحقيقي ضروري
records.attribution: Taftazani embedded lemmas within Sanandaji commentary
notes: I075.upper.01.
records.stage86_prior_english_analytic_draft: “In a real composite it is necessary that some of its parts depend on others.” If each component were independent of every other one, no **single genuine compound** would arise from their aggregation. The argument proceeds on I:75 by distinguishing unity produced by a real form from the merely conceived unity of an aggregate.
records.stage86_source_note: Source-bound claim; proof and different kinds of composition still open.
records.stage86_copytext: Būlāq 1318 AH, printed Volume I:74, physical combined PDF p.87
records.stage86_attribution_policy: Upper, ruled and lower voices retained separately; no unassigned note is attributed to Wasīm

records.title: Substrate, multiplicity, and a contested regress
records.arabic_anchors: «أن يوجد فيه وحدات ويلزم منه انتهاء المعروض المتعدد إلى المعروض الواحد» · «لكن لا يلزم الانتهاء إلى البسيط بمعنى ما لا جزء له» · «بل جواز أن يكون ذلك المعروض الواحد مركبا» · «فتلزم كون العوارض بسائط بالمعنى المذكور ولكنه ليس هو المدعى».
records.english: If there is a multiplicity of unities in a subject, it is argued that an underlying plurality must ultimately terminate at a **single bearer** of those predications. The marginal commentator concedes that this may establish some kind of unity, but denies that it necessarily establishes an **absolutely simple thing having no parts**. The single bearer might itself be composite under a different analysis. That would mean only that the accidents considered in relation to it are simple under the restricted sense just given, not that the bearer is simple in the absolute sense intended by the proof. The inference therefore moves from *a unified subject* to *an indivisible quiddity* without sufficient justification.

records.title: The mistaken derivation of simplicity from intellectual composition
records.arabic_anchors: «وقد يستدل على انتهاء المركب العقلي إلى البسيط بأنه لو لم ينته إليه لامتنع تعقل الماهية» · «لامتناع إحاطة العقل بما لا يتناهى» · «فإن معنى المركب العقلي هو ما لا يكون تمايز أجزائه إلا بحسب العقل».
records.english: Another argument says that intellectual compounds must terminate in something simple; otherwise the intellect could not grasp a quiddity, since it cannot encompass an infinite number of constituents. The objection is that this misconstrues **intellectual composition**. Its parts are distinguished *by the intellect's analysis*, and it does not follow that the intellect must successively traverse an actually infinite multitude of separately real things in order to apprehend the whole. The conclusion would require an additional demonstration that the distinction of conceptual constituents implies a corresponding multiplicity which must be completed in actual cognition.

records.title: Unity of real composition, and a warning about “material” parts
records.arabic_anchors: «(قوله وحدة حقيقية الخ) للقطع بأنه لا يحصل من الحجر الموضوع بجنب الإنسان مثلا واحد حقيقي» · «(قوله من الجانبين) أي لكن لا باعتبار واحد وإلا لزم الدور» · «(قوله كذا قالوا) إشارة إلى أن مبناه على قواعدهم» · «(قوله قلنا الصورة الاجتماعية) حاصل الجواب».
records.english: On “A genuine unity”: there can plainly be no genuine single being made merely by placing a stone beside a human being. On “On both sides”: the dependence must not be asserted **under a single and identical respect**, since that would yield circularity. On “Thus they say”: the expression reports the philosophers' principles rather than presenting them as a demonstration without remaining questions. On “We reply: the collective form”: the answer is that one must distinguish the **constitution of a real composite** from an intellectual consideration of togetherness. If “dependence” is said to concern the material constituents of genuine compounds, the claim is not automatically true of every aggregation of physical things. What needs proving is dependence among the **really existing constituents and the form** that makes them one. The next lower gloss takes up this point and qualifies the relation to the producer.
notes: I076.lower.01.

records.title: Genuine unity and asymmetric dependence between parts
records.arabic_anchors: «ماهية واحدة ووحدة حقيقية» · «ثم الاحتياج فيما بين الجزأين قد يكون من جانب واحد كالتركيب من البسائط العنصرية» · «وعاما قد يكون من الصور المعدنية والنباتية والحيوانية إذ الصورة تحتاج إلى تلك المواد من غير عكس» · «وقد يكون من الجانبين كاحتياج الهيولى إلى الصورة وهن احتياج الصورة إلى الهيولى».
records.english: “One quiddity and a genuine unity.”
records.arabic: ماهية واحدة ووحدة حقيقية
records.attribution: Taftazani embedded lemmas within Sanandaji commentary
records.stage86_prior_english_analytic_draft: —[Otherwise the components would not give] one quiddity and a genuine unity. Dependence between two constituents can sometimes run **one way only**, as in a compound of elemental simples. The forms involved in minerals, plants, and animals require their material substrata, without the opposite dependence necessarily following in the same sense. Or dependence may run **both ways**, as with prime matter and form: matter requires form, while form too requires matter in the relevant kind of corporeal composition. These examples distinguish the relation of ontological dependence from mere juxtaposition.
records.stage86_source_note: Phrase at the transition of the real-composition argument.
records.stage86_copytext: Būlāq 1318 AH, printed Volume I:75, physical combined PDF p.88
records.stage86_attribution_policy: Upper, ruled and lower voices retained separately; no unassigned note is attributed to Wasīm

records.title: Why the collective form of an army is not another produced thing
records.arabic_anchors: «(بخلاف المركب الاعتباري)» · «فإن قيل احتياج الهيئة الاجتماعية إلى الأجزاء المادية لازم قطعًا» · «قلنا الصورة الاجتماعية في المركبات الاعتبارية محض اعتبار العقل».
records.english: “Unlike a merely conceptual composite.”
records.arabic: بخلاف المركب الاعتباري
records.attribution: Taftazani embedded lemmas within Sanandaji commentary
notes: I076.upper.01.
records.stage86_prior_english_analytic_draft: “Unlike a considerational composite.” If it is objected that the **collective configuration** surely depends upon the material components that constitute it, we reply that the collective form of a merely considerational composite is **nothing but a consideration of the intellect**. It is not established as an additional extramental entity needing a cause in the same manner as a substantial form. This is why dependence of a genuine compound cannot be inferred directly from the need of an army for its soldiers or the need of an aggregation for its members. The next page develops the point explicitly through the army example.
records.stage86_source_note: Short opening of the army/collective-whole objection and response.
records.stage86_copytext: Būlāq 1318 AH, printed Volume I:75, physical combined PDF p.88
records.stage86_attribution_policy: Upper, ruled and lower voices retained separately; no unassigned note is attributed to Wasīm

records.title: The lower commentator objects to how the debate is framed
records.arabic_anchors: «الاجتماعية في المركب الاعتباري ليست موجودة في الخارج» · «مثل الترياق والسكنجبين مركبا حقيقيا» · «فإنه يحدث بتركيبه صورة في نفس الأمر» · «المركب الحقيقي من الجوهر والعرض» · «كالنفس والبدن للإنسان» · «(قوله إن المراد من المجعولية الخ)».
records.english: The collective character of a **considerational composite** is not present externally. But if someone asks how a **real composite** is possible, consider a compound medicine such as *tiryāq* or *sakanjabīn*: through the composition, a form really arises and the components require that form as a principle or source. Even if the emergent form is granted to be a substantial form, the result does not by itself settle the special case of a composite constructed of accidents. One can only say that a real composite of substance and accident is possible if its constitutive relation is established—not that every aggregation must have the status of a genuine unity. The note also directs us to examples of genuinely existing constituent parts: soul and body in a human being; or such oppositions as necessity of existence and impossibility of nonexistence, which must not be confused with merely verbal enumeration. On “What is meant by made-ness, etc.” a previous author/commentator's account is introduced, and its full continuation is on I:77.
notes: A short expression following the medicinal examples is compressed in the scan. The translation conveys the explicit comparison but does not introduce an unprinted substantial form as an established conclusion. The marginal stream continues across I076→I077.

records.title: A separately ruled correction to the reading of “concomitant of existence”
records.arabic_anchors: «(قوله من لوازم الوجود الخ) يعني ليس مراد المخالف أن الصادر عن الفاعل هو الوجود دون الماهية».
records.english: On “among the concomitants of existence”: The opponent does not mean that what proceeds from the agent is existence rather than quiddity: existence, on this view, is an intellectual consideration and does not need a maker. He means that what is made is quiddity under a qualification—that is, qualified quiddity—which requires an agent, unlike quiddity taken in itself. This is also what the advocate of quiddity’s being made intends, so the dispute comes down to wording. [End of the printed ruled note.]
records.arabic: (قوله من لوازم الوجود إلخ) يعني ليس مراد المخالف أن الصادر عن الفاعل هو الوجود دون الماهية، فإن الوجود أمر اعتباري لا يحتاج إلى جاعل، بل مراده أن المجعول هو الماهية بشرط شيء، أعني الماهية المخلوطة، فإنها التي تحتاج إلى فاعل دون الماهية من حيث هي، كما أنها المرادة عند القائل بمجعوليتها، فيكون النزاع راجعاً إلى اللفظ. اه منه.
notes: This note is bounded by two horizontal rules. Do not conflate it with either the upper sharḥ or the long lower ḥāshiya.
records.stage92_prior_working_overview: On “Among the concomitants of existence, etc.” What the opponent means is **not** that what issues from the agent is existence without quiddity, as though existence were an external, self-subsisting entity and quiddity wholly excluded from the act of production. Existence is a matter of consideration, needing no agent considered as an independent entity. Rather, the point is that what is produced is quiddity **on condition that it is mixed with existence**. Under that description it requires an agent; it does not follow that the unqualified quiddity, considered apart from existence, likewise requires one. The dispute may thus turn on the *wording* or on which consideration of quiddity is intended. [The printed attribution/signature at the close is a reference to a prior discussion, not a securely identified individual author.]

stage92_source_note.witness: Būlāq 1318 AH printed Volume I (single printed copy, no manuscript collation)
stage92_source_note.scope: entire visually bounded ruled note, first transcription pass
stage92_source_note.limitations: A complete short printed ruled note on the agent and qualified quiddity, first-pass transcription only, without independent second proof.

records.title: On what can be externally real, and the status of collective unity
records.arabic_anchors: «لا تحقق لها في الخارج إذ ليس من العسكر في الخارج إلا تلك الأفراد» · «ولو جعلت الهيئة جزءا من العسكر لم يكن العسكر أمرا موجودا في الخارج لأن ما جزؤه عدمي فهو عدمي» · «ثم اعلم أنهم اختلفوا في الماهيات الممكنة أهي مجعولة الجاعل أم لا».
records.english: “It has no realization outside the mind, since the army as externally existing consists of nothing beyond those individuals.”
records.arabic: لا تحقق لها في الخارج إذ ليس من العسكر في الخارج إلا تلك الأفراد
records.attribution: Taftazani embedded lemmas within Sanandaji commentary
notes: incoming I075.upper.final. The boundary between the last sentence about the collective form and the heading on possible quiddities is a transition in the printed main argument.
records.stage86_prior_english_analytic_draft: —There is no realization of it in the external world, for what exists externally of an army is nothing beyond its individual soldiers. If the collective configuration is made a constituent of the army, the army would no longer be an externally existing thing, since a thing one of whose constituents is non-existent is itself non-existent. Know, then, that they have differed about possible quiddities: are they things produced by an agent, or not? This is another disputed question, and the author has chosen to express it in terms of whether the possible thing needs an agent, for that is one of the concomitants of [being] a quiddity or of [the way it is treated as] produced. The difference in formulation must not be flattened into the claim that the author has already determined the issue.
records.stage86_source_note: Part of a longer argument distinguishing conceptual and real composites.
records.stage86_copytext: Būlāq 1318 AH, printed Volume I:76, physical combined PDF p.89
records.stage86_attribution_policy: Upper, ruled and lower voices retained separately; no unassigned note is attributed to Wasīm

records.title: What is meant by the claim that quiddity is not made
records.arabic_anchors: «(ومن ثالث في مجعولية الماهية)» · «فقال بمجعولية الماهية أراد أنها تعرض للماهية في الجملة» · «ومن ثالث في مجعولية الماهية» · «(أراد أنها) أي المجعولية (من لوازم الوجود) وعوارض الهوية (كتناهي الأجسام) فإنه ليس».
records.english: [The text] introduces a third disagreement about the *made-ness* (*majʿūliyya*) of a quiddity. The position denying that quiddity is produced concerns whether made-ness is attributed to quiddity as such, or whether it belongs to the quiddity only under a certain consideration. In explaining what was intended by the expression, the discussion identifies made-ness with the concomitants of existence and the accidents of concrete actuality, as in the finitude of bodies. The comparison extends into I:77; it should not be read as an argument that bodies themselves, or their quiddities considered in isolation, are independently created as distinct additional entities.
records.attribution: Taftazani embedded lemmas within Sanandaji commentary
notes: The compressed typography in the clause before «أراد أنها» requires a separate line-level proof. The English here preserves the reported issue but is **interpretive at that exact point**, not a certified literal rendering.
outgoing I077.upper.01.

records.title: Whether the need is for an agent or for something other than the composite
records.arabic_anchors: «إن المجعولية قد يراد بها الاحتياج إلى الفاعل وقد يراد بها الاحتياج إلى الغير على ما يعم الجزء أيضا» · «وكلاهما من عوارض الممكن» · «الأول من لوازم هويته مطلقا والثاني من لوازم ماهية المركب دون البسيط».
records.english: “Made-ness” may mean dependence on a producing agent; it may also mean dependence on something **other than itself**, in a sense broad enough to include dependence on a constituent part. Both are attributes of the possible thing. The first, however, is a concomitant of its concrete actuality, while the second pertains to the quiddity of a composite rather than that of a simple thing. Thus the word “made” is liable to equivocation unless the kind of dependence is determined.

records.title: Qualification of the alleged merely verbal dispute
records.arabic_anchors: «(قوله فعلى ما ذكر يكون الخلاف لفظيا)» · «أقول هذه المسألة ... كما أشار إليه الشارح» · «لا تكاد تنضبط مذاهب المتكلمين» · «الماهيات بسيطة كانت أو مركبة تجعل الجاعل» · «جمهور الفلاسفة إلى أنها ليست بجعل الجاعل مطلقا».
records.english: On “On what has been stated, the disagreement would be merely verbal”: I say that the question is not so easily brought under a single formula. The positions and terms used by the theologians are not readily reduced to one pattern. Some hold that quiddities, whether simple or composite, are produced by an agent, even where this requires acknowledging the production of a composite without separately producing its parts. The majority of philosophers are reported to hold that quiddities as such are not products of an agent in any unqualified sense; others distinguish simple from composite quiddities or disagree over whether a composite needs a producer by virtue of its parts. The commentator is warning that the seemingly verbal disagreement overlays several distinct propositions.
notes: The marginal enumeration and attribution of positions must be checked against the full preceding and following notes before assigning a view to a named school.

records.title: The objection about an independently produced quiddity
records.arabic_anchors: «فإن معنى المركب العقلي هو ما لا يكون تمايز أجزائه إلا بحسب العقل» · «ولا يستلزم كونه معقولا بأجزائه» · «لو كان جعل الجاعل لزم في تقدير عدم الجاعل أن لا يكون الإنسان إنسانا» · «فإنه عند ارتفاع الجاعل يرتفع الموجود وتبقى الماهية معدومة».
records.english: The point is not answered by identifying an intellectual composite with a mere aggregate of separately existing things. A composite in the intellect is one whose components are differentiated by the intellect, and this need not entail separate actual existence for every intelligible constituent. The objector then says: if a producer makes the very quiddity of man, the removal of that producer would imply that a human being is no longer human. Two forms of the objection are considered. If this is a negative proposition, we do not concede that the quiddity of a human remains a subject about which that negative assertion could be made; the existent is removed with the producer, and the quiddity is left without external existence. If the claim is understood as one about the intelligible essence independently of the act of existing, the answer differs. The argument continues at the opening of I:78.
notes: outgoing I078.lower.01.

records.title: Possible quiddities and the four-element example
records.arabic_anchors: «من لوازم ماهية الجسم حتى لو تصورنا جسما غير متناه كان جسما» · «(لا من لوازم الماهية كزوجية الأربعة)» · «فإنها من لوازم ماهية الأربعة حتى إذا تصورنا الأربعة ليست بزوج لم تكن أربعة» · «(وإلا) يكن مراد المخالف ما ذكر لكن (كان احتياج الممكن إلى العلة ضروريا)».
records.english: “Not among the concomitants of the quiddity—unlike the evenness of four, which is a concomitant of the quiddity of four.”
records.arabic: لا من لوازم الماهية كزوجية الأربعة فإنها من لوازم ماهية الأربعة
records.attribution: Taftazani embedded lemmas within Sanandaji commentary
notes: incoming I076.upper.02, outgoing I078.upper.01 (new chapter on individuation).
records.stage86_prior_english_analytic_draft: —[Bodily finitude belongs among the concomitants of the existence of body,] not the concomitants of the very quiddity of body: even if we imagined an infinite body, it would still be a body. “It is not like the evenness of four,” which belongs to the quiddity of four: if four were conceived as not even, it would not be four. “Otherwise”—if the opponent did not mean the distinction just mentioned, and instead denied that possible quiddities require an agent even under the relevant existential consideration—“the possible thing’s need of a cause would be necessary.” On the author's clarification, that would render the dispute only verbal; further investigation of the reality of existence and quiddity is therefore postponed to its proper place.
records.stage86_source_note: Boundary clause; contrast of bodily finitude with numerical evenness is more extensive in the print.
records.stage86_copytext: Būlāq 1318 AH, printed Volume I:77, physical combined PDF p.90
records.stage86_attribution_policy: Upper, ruled and lower voices retained separately; no unassigned note is attributed to Wasīm

records.title: Completion of the I:77 objection
records.arabic_anchors: «عند ارتفاع الجاعل لا يبقى الإنسان حتى يصح موضوعا للإيجاب» · «كذا في شرح المقاصد» · «وثانيا أن الوجود أو الاتصاف ماهية من الماهيات في القول بمجعوليتهما اعتراف بمجعوليته».
records.english: —When the producer is removed, there is no human being left to serve as the subject of an affirmative proposition. Such is the discussion in *Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid*, and it deserves examination. Secondly, existence itself, or the qualification of a thing by existence, is a quiddity among quiddities if treated as an intelligible object; to affirm that its existence or its qualification is produced is thus to concede the production of a quiddity [under that consideration]. One must therefore attend to what exactly is asserted when the debate is called verbal.
notes: incoming I077.lower.03.

records.title: Existence and determination: the disagreement is not just an argument over words
records.arabic_anchors: «فلا نزاع حقيقة وفيه أيضا نظر فإن النزاع في الماهيات التي هي حقائق الأشياء» · «لا فيما صدقت الماهية عليه من الأفراد» · «أكثر أدلة المتكلمين على تقدير تمامها أيضا لا تفيد إلا كون الوجود» · «بل اتصاف الماهية به من الفاعل في الحقيقة».
records.english: But there is a further difficulty. The actual controversy concerns **quiddities insofar as they are the realities of things**, not simply the individual things of which a quiddity is predicated. Most of the proofs offered by the theologians, even supposing them to be complete, would establish only that existence—or the attribution of existence to a quiddity—comes from an efficient agent. They do not, simply as they stand, show that the quiddity in its own right is also produced. The individual expressions can be verbally reinterpreted while the metaphysical issue remains unresolved.

records.title: What “shared” can mean in the claim about universals
records.arabic_anchors: «(قوله مشتركا بينه وبين غيره)» · «فإن المراد من اشتراك تلك الأمور أما اشتراك كليها بين الأشياء» · «ولكن منع عدم اشتراك التعين كذلك» · «وأما اشتراك أفرادها» · «فممنوع ضرورة أن الفرد الموجود من الوحدة مثلا في هذا الشيء غير الفرد الموجود في ذلك الشيء».
records.english: On “Shared between it and another.” The intended sharing may refer to the **universal notions** of these things being shared among particulars. But that would not establish that individuation as a universal notion is incapable of being shared—indeed, the text itself admits that it is a universal concept. Alternatively, the intended sharing may refer to **individual instances** of existence, unity, and quiddity. That reading is denied: the individual unity existing in this thing is not numerically the same individual unity existing in another. On either interpretation, the asserted contrast needs further clarification.

records.title: Individual unity and a generic universal: the force of the objection
records.arabic_anchors: «فإن كل شيء نوع منحصر في فرده» · «(قوله ولذا يصدق قولنا الكلي)» · «فإن عدم صدق قولنا الكلي متعين لا يقتضي عدم اشتراك التعين الذي بينه وبين غيره» · «إلا أن يشار بكلمة الإشارة إلى تعاير تلك الأمور».
records.english: More strictly, each thing can be considered as belonging to its own determinate kind under the relation in question; it is not established that all the individual marks of one thing coincide with those of another. On the sentence “Therefore we can say of the universal...,” the failure of “the universal is individuated” to be true does **not** entail that there is no shared *concept* of individuation predicable in discussing that universal and others. Perhaps the contrast becomes defensible only if the expression is being used demonstratively, to point to **this particular** individuation rather than the common notion of individuation. The commentator therefore challenges the proposed inference, rather than simply repeating it.
notes: The last phrase continues beyond the bottom of I:78 into I:79’s lower margin; its exact syntactic scope requires a joined proof. No unprinted conclusion is supplied.

records.title: Chapter on individuation (*taʿayyun*)
records.arabic_anchors: «فصل في التعين» · «تعين الشيء كما في شرح المقاصد غير ماهيته ووجوده ووحدته» · «لتكون كل من هذه الأمور مشتركا بينه وبين غيره بخلاف التعين» · «ولذا صدق قولنا الكلي ماهية وهو موجود وواحد» · «ولا يصدق أنه متعين وإن كان التعين مفهوما كليا».
records.english: “Section: On Individuation … the individuation of a thing, as stated in Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid, is other than its quiddity, existence and unity.”
records.arabic: فصل في التعين … تعين الشيء كما في شرح المقاصد غير ماهيته ووجوده ووحدته
records.attribution: Taftazani embedded lemmas within Sanandaji commentary
notes: outgoing I079.upper.01 (“as applicable to many...”). The top register on I:78 ends mid-sentence.
records.stage86_prior_english_analytic_draft: **Chapter on individuation.** The individuation of a thing, as stated in *Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid*, is other than its quiddity, its existence, and its unity. Each of those—quiddity, existence, and unity—can be shared in some way by a thing and another thing; **individuation**, by contrast, is what prevents that shared predication. Thus we can truthfully say that a universal has a quiddity, is existent [under the relevant sense of existence], and is one, but we cannot predicate individuation of the universal as such—even though *individuation* is itself a universal concept, as explained by what follows.
records.stage86_source_note: Heading plus opening thesis, not the remainder of the individuation discussion.
records.stage86_copytext: Būlāq 1318 AH, printed Volume I:78, physical combined PDF p.91
records.stage86_attribution_policy: Upper, ruled and lower voices retained separately; no unassigned note is attributed to Wasīm

records.arabic: التغاير فتدبر فالأولى هو ما في شرح المقاصد (قوله عموم من وجه) ولعل ذلك مبني على أنهم يريدون من التعين كون الشيء بحيث يصير مانعا من حمله على كثيرين ومن التميز كون الشيء بحيث ينفرد عن مشاركاته فالمعتبر في الأول كونه جزئيا سواء كان مع اعتبار المشاركة أو لا وفي الثاني التمايز عن المشارك سواء كان في الجزئي أو لا
records.english: —difference. Reflect: the preferable account is therefore that in Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid. On “Overlap without either wholly including the other.” This may rest on their meaning by determination that a thing is such as to prevent its predication of many, and by distinction that it is set apart from things sharing with it. What matters in the first is its being particular, whether or not sharing is considered; in the second, its being distinguished from something sharing with it, whether or not the distinction occurs at the level of a particular.
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: (قوله في أن التعين وجودي أو عدمي الخ) قد يقال أمر اعتباري لا تحقق له في الأعيان إذ لو كان موجودا في الخارج كان له تعين وهكذا فيتسلسل وقد يجاب بأنه إنما يلزم ذلك لو كانت التعينات متشاركة في الماهية لتحتاج في التمايز إلى التعين لم لا يجوز أن تكون مختلفة الماهية متمايزة بالذات وإنما تتشارك في لفظ التعين أو في عرضي لها هو مفهوم التعين
records.english: On “Whether determination is existential or privative, etc.” It may be said that determination is a matter of consideration, with no realization among external things: if it existed externally, it would have a determination of its own, and so on without end. The reply may be that this follows only if determinations share a quiddity, requiring another determination to distinguish them. Why could they not have different quiddities and be intrinsically distinct, sharing only the word “determination” or an accidental feature, namely the concept of determination?
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: وأما حديث كون تعين التعين نفسه فقد قيل إنه مدفوع بأن ذلك الاتحاد إنما يصح في الأمور الاعتبارية كالحدوث ونحوه وأما التعين فهو من الأمور الخارجية العارضة للعين في الخارج وتغاير العارض والمعروض الخارجيين ضروري كذا في شرح المقاصد لكن فيه تأمل لا يخفى كما سيأتي
records.english: As for the claim that a determination’s determination is itself, it has been said that this is refuted by the fact that such identity is valid only in matters of consideration, such as origination and the like. Determination, by contrast, is an external thing attaching to an entity externally, and an external attribute and its external bearer are necessarily different. This is what is stated in Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid. But it plainly calls for examination, as will become clear.
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: وقد يقال إنه وجودي لأنه جزء المتعين إذ هو عبارة عن الماهية والتعين وهو موجود وجزء الموجود موجود ورد بأنه لم لا يجوز أن يكون المتعين هو نحو الإنسان المقيد بالعوارض المشخصة دون المجموع ولو سلم فهم لا يسلمون كون تلك العوارض الموجودة تعينا بل ما به التعين
records.english: It may also be said that determination is existential because it is a part of the determined thing, which consists of quiddity and determination. The determined thing exists, and a part of what exists also exists. The objection is: why could the determined thing not be, for example, the human being qualified by individuating accidents, rather than the aggregate [of that subject and those accidents]? Even if this is granted, they do not concede that those existing accidents are determination itself; rather, they are that through which determination occurs.
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: صادقا على الكثرة وبين التعين والتميز عموم من وجه لصدقهما على مشخصات الأفراد إذ المعتبر مشاركتها في الماهية مثلا فإن كلا منها متشخص في نفسه ومتميز عن غيره وصدق التعين دون التميز حيث لا تعتبر المشاركة وبالعكس على تميز الكليات كالأنواع المعتبر اشتراكها في الجنس هذا ثم اعلم أنه اختلف في أن التعين وجودي أو عدمي حقيقي أو اعتباري فلا بد في تحقيق أنه ما هو من بيان ما هو المراد من هذه الألفاظ فنقول (أفراد النوع إما تتمايز بعوارض ربما تنتهي) تلك العوارض
records.english: —as applying to many. Determination and distinction overlap without either wholly including the other. Both apply to the individuating features of individuals when, for example, their sharing in a quiddity is taken into account: each is individuated in itself and distinct from the other. Determination applies without distinction where sharing is not taken into account. Conversely, distinction applies without determination to the distinction between universals, such as species considered as sharing in a genus. Having established this, know that there is disagreement over whether determination is existential or privative, real or merely a matter of consideration. To establish what it is, we must therefore explain what these expressions mean. We say: “The individuals of a species are either distinguished by accidents which may terminate”—those accidents may terminate—
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: (قوله إلى ما يفيد الهاذية الخ) لعله أراد بما يفيدها كون الفرد بحيث لا يقبل الشركة (قوله وامتناع الشركة) عطف تفسير للهاذية (قوله أي العوارض نفسها) تفسير ما لا تفسير ضمير المفعول فإنه للهاذية وتخصيص ما يفيد بالعوارض مع أنها مفيد بعيد إنما لتصريح بعده بالمفيد القريب أعني كون الفرد بحيث لا يقبل الشركة فتدبر
records.english: On “In what produces thisness, etc.” Perhaps by what produces it he means the individual’s being such that it does not admit sharing. On “And the impossibility of sharing.” This is an explanatory coordination clarifying “thisness.” On “Namely the accidents themselves.” This explains “what,” not the object pronoun, which refers to thisness. “What produces it” is specified as the accidents, although they are a remote producer, only because the proximate producer is explicitly stated afterward: the individual’s being such that it does not admit sharing. Reflect.
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: (قوله أي أن يشترك فيه) أي معنى التعين هو كون الفرد بحيث يمتنع أن يشترك فيه أفراد أي يمتنع أن يحمل على كثيرين لا كونه بحيث لا يشترك مع غيره في شيء إذ لا متعين من إلا وهو له شريك في أمر كلي فافهم
records.english: On “That several things share in it.” The meaning of determination is that the individual is such that several individuals cannot share in it—that is, it cannot be predicated of many. It does not mean that it shares nothing with anything else, for every determinate thing has something else sharing with it in a universal feature. Understand.

readings.status: The small word من between متعين and إلا appears extraneous or damaged. The clear assertion is that every determinate thing shares some universal feature; no missing Arabic is supplied.

records.arabic: (قوله المركب مع وجودي الخ) أي المعتبر على طريق العدم والملكة (قوله أو غير المركب) أي المعتبر على طريق الإيجاب والسلب
records.english: On “Compounded with an existential element, etc.” That is, considered in terms of privation and possession. On “Or uncompounded.” That is, considered in terms of affirmation and negation.
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: (إلى ما يفيد الهاذية) وامتناع الشركة كذا إذا كانت الأفراد من الموجودات الخارجية (فبعد تلخيص أن) المراد من (التعين والتشخص هو تلك الهاذية) الحاصلة بالعوارض (أو ما يفيدها) أي العوارض نفسها (أو كون الفرد بحيث لا يقبل الشركة) أي أن يشترك فيه (أو عدم قبوله لها) أي للشركة
records.english: —“in what produces thisness” (hādhiyya) and the impossibility of sharing. This applies when the individuals are external existents. “After clarifying that” what is meant by “determination and individuation is that thisness” produced by the accidents, “or what produces it,” namely the accidents themselves, “or the individual’s being such that it does not admit sharing”—that is, that several things share in it—“or its not admitting it,” namely sharing—
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: (و) بعد تلخيص (أن) المراد بـ (العدمي هو العدم أو العدم) المطلق أو (المضاف) المركب مع وجودي كعدم البصر عما من شأنه أن يكون بصيرا أو غير المركب كعدم قبول الشركة (أو ما يدخل في مفهومه العدم) ككون الشيء بحيث لا يقبل الشركة (و) أن المراد من (الوجودي) ما كان (بخلافه) فهو الموجود أو الوجود مطلقا أو المضاف أو ما لا يدخل في مفهومه العدم والعبرة بالمعنى حتى إن العمى عدمي وإن اللاعمى وجودي
records.english: “And” after clarifying “that” what is meant by “privative is nonexistence, or nonexistence”—unrestricted or “relative,” compounded with an existential element, as with the absence of sight in what is capable of seeing; or uncompounded, as with not admitting sharing—“or that whose concept includes nonexistence,” as with a thing’s being such that it does not admit sharing; “and” that the “existential” is what is “opposed to it”: an existent, existence whether unrestricted or relative, or that whose concept does not include nonexistence. Meaning is what matters: blindness is privative, while non-blindness is existential.
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: (و) بعد تلخيص (أن) المراد من (الحقيقي ما له ثبوت في نفس الأمر) أي في حد ذاته (من غير شائبة فرض وتقدير) من العقل (و) أن المراد من (الاعتباري) ما كان (بخلافه) يعني ما لا تحقق له إلا بحسب فرض العقل (لا يشتبه أن التعين وجودي أو عدمي حقيقي أو اعتباري) فلا خفاء في أن العوارض وجودية والهاذية اعتبارية وكون الفرد بحيث لا يقبل الشركة أو عدم قبوله لها عدميان (و) أيضا (لا يشتبه) عليك (أنه) أي التعين لا يحصل بانضمام
records.english: “And” after clarifying “that” the “real is what is established in the thing itself”—in its own right—“without any admixture of supposition or positing” by the intellect, “and” that the “considerational” is what is “opposed to it,” meaning what has no realization except through intellectual supposition, “there is no ambiguity as to whether determination is existential or privative, real or considerational.” It is clear that the accidents are existential; thisness is considerational; and the individual’s being such that it does not admit sharing, or its not admitting sharing, are both privative. “And” it is also “not unclear” to you “that it”—determination—does not arise by adding—
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: (قوله لأن كلا من المنضم والمنضم إليه الخ) إن قيل حكم الكل قد يخالف حكم كل فيجوز أن يكون كل من المنضم والمنضم إليه كليا والمجموع جزئيا قلنا لا معنى للانضمام هاهنا سوى أن العقل يعتبر مفهوما كليا ثم يعتبر له وصفا كليا ومعلوم بالضرورة أن الكلي الموصوف بالأوصاف الكلية لا ينتهي إلى حد المادية وإن كان ذلك الوصف هو مفهوم الجزئية وامتناع قبول الشركة أو يقال مرادهم من نفي حصول التعين من ذلك الانضمام هو أن انضمام الكلي إلى الكلي لا يستلزم التعين والتشخص لا أنه لا يفيده أصلا فالمقصود أن المعنى الذي بسببه امتنع للعقل فرض صدق المفهوم على كثيرين لا بد أن يستند إلى أمر يستلزمه
records.english: On “For both what is added and what it is added to, etc.” If it is said that the whole may have a judgment different from that of each component, so that both components may be universal while the whole is particular, we reply: addition here means only that the intellect considers a universal concept and then considers a universal attribute of it. It is necessarily known that a universal qualified by universal attributes does not thereby reach [the limit designated by a word read provisionally as “materiality”], even when the attribute is the concept of particularity or of the impossibility of sharing. Alternatively, one may say that, in denying that determination arises from such addition, their intention is that adding one universal to another does not entail determination and individuation: not that it never produces them at all. The intended point is that the factor because of which the intellect cannot suppose a concept to apply to many must depend on something that entails that factor.
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

readings.status: The noun is provisionally read المادية (materiality). The argument concerns particularity; no conjectural replacement has been inserted.

proof_notes: I081_lower_second.png resolves لا أنه: lack of entailment is not a denial of every instance of production.

records.arabic: (قال فهو إما مستند إلى الفاعل القادر الخ) فهو الموجد مستندا لكل ما شاء من التشخصات على ما سيأتي تفصيله (قوله لا يفيد العلية) أي فيجوز أن الوجود ما معه التعين لا ما هو علة التعين
records.english: He says, “It therefore depends either on a powerful agent, etc.” He is the originator, serving as the ground of whichever individuations He wills, as will be explained in detail. On “Does not establish causation.” That is, existence may be that with which determination occurs, rather than that which causes determination.

records.arabic: (٦ ـ تقريب أول)
records.english: [Printing/signature mark:] “6 — Taqrīb, first [part].”

records.arabic: الكلي إلى الكلي لأن كلا من المنضم والمنضم إليه يمكن للعقل فرض صدقه على كثيرين والتعين على كل تقدير لا بد فيه من كون المفهوم بحيث لا يمكن للعقل ذلك (فهو إما مستند إلى الفاعل القادر) المختار كغيره من الممكنات على ما هو عندنا من استناد الكل إليه تعالى (أو إلى الوجود الخارجي) عند بعض للقطع بأن الماهية إذا تحققت في الخارج لا تقبل الشركة وإنما تقبلها في العقل
records.english: —one universal to another. For the intellect can suppose both what is added and what it is added to as applying to many. Determination, on any account, requires the concept to be such that the intellect cannot do that. “It therefore depends either on a powerful agent” acting by choice, as other possible things do, according to our position that everything depends on Him, exalted is He, “or on external existence,” according to some. For we are certain that a quiddity, when realized externally, does not admit sharing; it admits sharing only in the intellect.
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: فإن قيل فيلزم أن لا يتعدد التعين لأن الوجود أمر واحد ومقتضى الواحد لا يكون إلا واحدا أجيب أن الوجود وإن كان بحسب المفهوم واحدا لكن تتعدد أفراده بحسب الأزمنة والأمكنة وسائر الأسباب وبعد اعترض بأن الدوران لا يفيد العلية فإن قيل نحن نقطع بالعلية عند الوجود الخارجي مع قطع النظر عن جميع ما عداه
records.english: If it is objected that determination would then not be multiple, because existence is one thing and what one thing entails can only be one, the answer is that existence, although one in concept, has multiple instances according to times, places and other causes. A further objection is that concomitant occurrence does not establish causation. If it is said, “We are certain of causation when external existence is present, without considering anything besides it”—
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: (قوله لا يوجب انتفاءه) وبالجملة عند الوجود لا بد من أمر يستند إليه الوجود فيجوز أن يستند إليه التعين أيضا ولو سلم فالوجود لا يقتضي إلا تعينا ما والكلام في التعينات المخصوصة فلا يثبت المطلوب اللهم إلا أن وجود كل فرد يقتضي تعينه الخاص
records.english: On “Does not entail its absence.” In sum, when existence obtains, there must be something on which it depends. Determination may also depend on that same thing. Even if the premise is granted, existence entails only some determination, whereas the discussion concerns specific determinations; the desired conclusion is therefore not established—unless it is said that the existence of each individual entails its own particular determination.
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: (قوله كما ذهب إليه الفلاسفة الخ) حاصل ما ذهبوا إليه على ما يستفاد من شرح المقاصد هو أن الموجود إما مادي أو غيره والثاني إما واجب كالباري أو ممكن وهو العقل والأول إما مادي في ذاته كالأجسام والأعراض أو مادي في التعلق كالنفوس البشرية والفلكية فغير المادي بقسميه تعينه مستند إلى نفس ماهيته فتنحصر كل ماهية في فرد لكن العقول لما كانت مختلفة الماهيات متعددة عندهم تعدد أفرادها وكل فرد منها لنوع من الماهية انحصرت فيه بخلاف الواجب فإن ماهيته لما لم تكن متعددة بل واحدة انحصرت في فرد واحد ولم يتصور هناك تعدد أصلا لا بحسب الفرد ولا بحسب النوع والمادي بنوعيه تعينه مستند إلى المادة أي محله والمراد به كما فصله بعضهم المعروض في الأعراض والمادة في الأجسام والمتعلق في النفوس بناء على ما ذكروا من حدوث النفس بعد البدن وتعينها به
records.english: On “As the philosophers hold, etc.” The substance of their position, as understood from Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid, is this. An existent is either material or otherwise. The latter is either necessary, like the Creator, or possible, namely an intellect. The former is either material in itself, like bodies and accidents, or material in its attachment, like human and celestial souls. Both kinds of non-material existent derive determination from their own quiddity, so each quiddity is confined to one individual. But since the intellects, on their account, have diverse and multiple quiddities, their individuals are multiple; each individual belongs to a species of quiddity confined to it. The Necessary Existent is different: since His quiddity is not multiple but one, it is confined to a single individual, and no multiplicity can be conceived there, whether of individuals or of species. Both kinds of material existent derive their determination from matter, that is, their subject. As some have explained in detail, this means the bearer in the case of accidents, matter in bodies, and the object of attachment in souls. The last rests on their claim that the soul comes into being after the body and is determined by it.
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: إذا عرفت هذا عرفت أن في تحرير الشارح «مد ظله» نوع اضطراب فإن قوله فينحصر نوعها في الشخص الواحد إلى قوله هذا إذا كان تعين الماهية زائدا عليها الخ لبيان استناد تعين المجردات كالعقول إلى ماهيتها فحينئذ إما أن يريد بقوله وأما إذا كانت الماهية متعينة في ذاتها الخ بيان أن ماهية الواجب مغايرة ماهية المجردات في أن تعينها ليس معللا بها زائدا عليها بل هو نفسها كما هو الظاهر من السياق مع أنه
records.english: Once you understand this, you will see a certain inconsistency in the commentator’s formulation—may his protection endure. His words from “Its species is then confined to the single individual” to “This applies when the quiddity’s determination is additional to it, etc.” explain how the determination of separate entities, such as intellects, depends on their quiddities. His subsequent words, “But when the quiddity is determined in its very essence, etc.,” must then intend either to explain that the Necessary Existent’s quiddity differs from that of separate entities, in that its determination is not additional to it and caused by it, but is the quiddity itself, as the context appears to suggest—although that—
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: قلنا قطع النظر عن الشيء لا يوجب انتفاءه (أو إلى أسباب أخر) كما ذهب إليه الفلاسفة من أن التعين قد يستند إلى (نفس الماهية) فينحصر نوعها في الشخص الواحد الحاصل من الماهية والتعين الذي علل بها لم يمكن أن يوجد معها تعين آخر وإلا انفك عنها التعين الأول فيتخلف المعلول عن علته هذا إذا كان تعين الماهية زائدا عليها معللا بها وأما إذا كانت الماهية متعينة في ذاتها ممتنعة في نفسها عن فرض الاشتراك فيها كالواجب تعالى على رأيهم فلا يتصور هناك تعدد أصلا
records.english: We reply: not considering something does not entail its absence. “Or [determination depends] on other causes,” as the philosophers hold. Determination may depend on “the quiddity itself.” Its species is then confined to the single individual consisting of the quiddity and the determination caused by it. No other determination can exist along with that quiddity; otherwise the first determination would be separated from it, and the effect would fail to accompany its cause. This applies when the quiddity’s determination is additional to it and caused by it. But when the quiddity is determined in its very essence, itself precluding the supposition of being shared—as with the Necessary Existent, exalted is He, on their account—no multiplicity can be conceived there at all.

readings.status: The print runs the clauses together. Punctuation in the translation distinguishes the single individual from the subsequent denial of another determination; no Arabic words are supplied.

records.arabic: خلاف ما ذهبوا إليه هناك كما مر آنفا يرد عليه أنه مع القول زيادة تعينها عليها وكونه معللا بها لم يتم القول بأنه لا يتصور هناك تعدد لا فردا ولا نوعا كما سبق إلا أن يقال المراد أنه حينئذ لا يتصور تعدد لا ذهنا ولا خارجا على ما صرح به المصنف في شرح المقاصد من أن قولهم أن لكل موجود ماهية كلية في العقل وإن امتنع تعدد أفرادها في الخارج مخصوص بغير الواجب تعالى فإنه في حقه محل نظر فتأمل
records.english: —is contrary to their position in that discussion, as just explained. The objection to him is that, while maintaining that its determination is additional to it and caused by it, the assertion that no multiplicity can be conceived there, whether individual or specific, does not follow in the manner stated—unless the intention is that multiplicity cannot then be conceived either mentally or externally. The author explicitly states in Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid that their claim, “Every existent has a universal quiddity in the intellect, even if it cannot have multiple external individuals,” applies only to what is other than the Necessary Existent, exalted is He; in His case, it is open to examination. Reflect.
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: وإما أن يريد به بيان أنها معادلة ماهية المجردات في امتناع تعدد أفرادها مطلقا وإن كان تعينها معللا بها أيضا كان حق العبارة أن يقول هذا إذا كانت الماهية مختلفة متنوعة وأما إذا كانت متحدة كالواجب تعالى فلا يتصور هناك الخ فتفطن فإن الإمساك من تحقيق أمثال هذا المقام ليس بسبيل الكرام
records.english: Or he intends to explain that it is on a par with the quiddity of separate entities in the absolute impossibility of multiple individuals, even if its determination is likewise caused by it. In that case the formulation should have been: “This applies when the quiddity is diverse and differentiated into species. But when it is one, as with the Necessary Existent, exalted is He, no multiplicity can be conceived there,” and so forth. Attend carefully: refraining from investigating matters of this kind is not the way of noble scholars.
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: (قوله من العوارض المتعينة في نفسها الخ) إشارة إلى جواب ما اعترض عليه من أن تعين الأعراض الحالة في المادة إنما هو بتعين المادة على ما سيجيء فلو تعينت المادة بها كان دورا وحاصل الجواب أن تعين المادة إنما هو بنفس الأعراض المتعينة بنفسها تعينا لا بتعيناتها المحلية الحاصلة بتعين المادة فلا دور ولا حصول التشخص بانضمام الكلي إلا أنه يرد أنه إذا جاز ذلك فلم لا يجوز تكثير الماهية وتعين أفرادها بما يلحقها من الأمور العارضة من غير لزوم مادة كذا قيل
records.english: On “By the accidents that are determinate in themselves, etc.” This points to the answer to an objection: accidents inhering in matter derive their determination from the determination of matter, as will be explained; were matter determined by them, circularity would follow. The substance of the answer is that matter is determined by the accidents themselves, which possess determination in themselves, not by their determinations as localized in a subject, which result from the determination of matter. There is therefore no circularity, nor does individuation arise by adding a universal. Nevertheless, the objection arises: if this is possible, why should a quiddity not be multiplied and its individuals determined through adventitious factors without requiring matter? So it has been said.
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

readings.status: The adjective read as المحلية is clear enough for a provisional rendering concerning localized determination, but remains a locus for comparison with a clearer witness.

records.arabic: (أو إلى المادة المتشخصة) إما بالذات كهيولات الأفلاك فإن هيولى كل فلك متشخصة في نفسها وممتازة عن هيولى فلك آخر وإما (بما يلحقها من العوارض) المتعينة في نفسها اللاحقة (بحسب تعاقب الاستعدادات) كهيولى العناصر الأربعة فإنها واحدة مشتركة بينها تشخصها وتعددها بما يعرض تلحقها بحسب تعاقب استعدادات مختلفة بحسب القرب والبعد من الفلك
records.english: “Or [determination depends] on individuated matter”: either matter individuated intrinsically, like the prime matters of the celestial spheres—for each sphere’s prime matter is individuated in itself and distinct from that of another sphere—or matter individuated “by the accidents that attach to it,” themselves determinate and attaching “according to successive dispositions.” An example is the prime matter of the four elements: it is one and shared among them; its individuation and multiplication arise through what attaches to it according to the succession of different dispositions, depending on proximity to, or distance from, the celestial sphere.

readings.status: The scan seems to have a compressed or faulty phrase. The translation gives the relation of adventitious accidents to matter, without silently restoring a new Arabic wording.

records.arabic: (قوله هي من الأمور العارضة للماهية الخ) قيل جعل الامتناع من لواحق الوجود والماهية إنما هو بالنظر إلى أن ضرورة سلب الوجود عن الماهية حال لهما أو إلى أنه من أوصاف الماهية المعقولة أو لكونه في مقابلة الإمكان
records.english: On “These are things that attach to a quiddity, etc.” It has been said that impossibility is counted among the concomitants of existence and quiddity either because the necessity of denying existence of a quiddity is a condition of the two; because it is an attribute of the conceived quiddity; or because it stands in opposition to possibility.
records.source_transcription_note: Manual reading of the supplied scan; punctuation and word spacing lightly normalized. Parentheses in the upper register retain printed lemma boundaries; this is not a diplomatic edition.

records.arabic: (قوله فإذا نسب المفهوم إلى وجوده الخ) أي إذا حمل الوجود في نفسه أو لأمر على مفهوم سواء بطريق الإيجاب أو السلب حصلت تلك المعاني فلا يرد أنها تحصل عند حمل العدم أو الربط بواسطته كما تحصل عند حمل الوجود كذلك وذلك لاندراجه فيما ذكرناه كما مر جوابه
records.english: On “When a concept is related to its existence, etc.” That is, when existence, whether in itself or for something, is predicated of a concept, affirmatively or negatively, those meanings arise. It is therefore no objection that they arise when nonexistence is predicated or used as the connecting term just as they arise when existence is predicated in that way. Such cases are included in what we have stated, as the answer has already explained.

records.arabic: فصل في بيان (الوجوب والامتناع والإمكان) هي من الأمور العارضة للماهية بالقياس إلى الوجود كالقدم والحدوث كما سيجيء إن شاء الله تعالى وهي (معقولات) أي معان عقلية (تحصل من نسبة المفهوم إلى هلية بسيطة) أي وجود في نفسه كأن يقال هل العنقاء موجود (أو مركبة) أي وجوده لأمر كأن يقال هل الحركة دائمة
records.english: Chapter explaining “necessity, impossibility and possibility.” These are things that attach to a quiddity in relation to existence, like eternity and origination, as will be explained, God willing. They are “intelligibles”—that is, intellectual meanings—“arising from relating a concept to a simple existential proposition,” namely existence in itself, as when one asks, “Does the phoenix exist?” “Or to a compound existential proposition,” namely its existence for something, as when one asks, “Is motion everlasting?”

records.arabic: قال في شرح المقاصد إن هل إما بسيطة يطلب بها الوجود الذي في نفسه أو مركبة يطلب بها وجود شيء لشيء فإذا نسب المفهوم إلى وجوده في نفسه أو وجوده لأمر حصل في العقل معان هي الوجوب والامتناع والإمكان لأن حمل الوجود على الشيء أو ربط الشيء بالشيء بواسطة الوجود إما على وجه الوجوب كقولنا صانع العالم موجود والأربعة يوجد لها الزوجية أو على وجه الامتناع كقولنا شريك الباري موجود والأربعة يوجد لها الفردية وإما على وجه الإمكان كقولنا الإنسان موجود أو يوجد له الكتابة ⟦والمغايرة لهما في هلية كل ما في كذا؟⟧
records.english: He says in Sharḥ al-Maqāṣid that a question with “whether” (hal) is either simple, asking about existence in itself, or compound, asking about one thing’s existence for another. When a concept is related to its existence in itself or its existence for something, intellectual meanings arise: necessity, impossibility and possibility. For existence is predicated of a thing, or one thing is connected with another by means of existence, either necessarily—as in “The Maker of the world exists” and “Evenness belongs to four”; impossibly—as in “A partner to the Creator exists” and “Oddness belongs to four”; or possibly—as in “A human being exists” or “Writing belongs to a human being.” [The final printed phrase concerning difference and existential predication is not securely read.]

records.arabic: (قوله يقصد به تفسير مدلول اللفظ الخ) ولهذا لا يتحاشى من أن يقال الواجب ما يمتنع عدمه والممتنع ما يجب عدمه والممكن ما لا يجب وجوده ولا عدمه ولا يمتنع وجوده ولا عدمه ولو كان القصد إلى إفادة تصور هذه المعاني لكان دورا ظاهرا
records.english: On “Its purpose is to explain what the expression signifies, etc.” For this reason one does not avoid saying: the necessary is that whose nonexistence is impossible; the impossible is that whose nonexistence is necessary; and the possible is that whose existence and nonexistence are neither necessary nor impossible. Had the purpose been to impart a conception of these meanings, the circularity would have been evident.

records.arabic: (قوله وعدم اجتماع النقيضين) مثال الامتناع الذاتي الحاصل من النسبة إلى الهلية البسيطة كالمثال الذي سبق وسيأتي أعني شريك الباري وههنا بحث لم أر من تعرض له وهو أن الامتناع المعقول هاهنا حاصل من نسبة وجود الاجتماع للنقيضين لا لوجود الاجتماع في نفسه فإن الاجتماع ليس ممتنعا في نفسه بل الممتنع إنما هو وجوده للنقيضين وكذا الشريك ليس ممتنعا في نفسه بل الممتنع إنما هو وجوده للباري فهما كامتناع الفردية للأربعة في الحصول من النسبة إلى الهلية المركبة مع اتفاقهم على تمثيلهما للهلية البسيطة
records.english: On “The non-occurrence of the conjunction of contradictories.” This is an example of intrinsic impossibility arising in relation to a simple existential proposition, like the earlier and forthcoming example of a partner to the Creator. There is a question here that I have not seen anyone address. The impossibility understood in this case arises from attributing conjunction to the contradictories, not from the existence of conjunction in itself. Conjunction is not impossible in itself; what is impossible is only its existence for the two contradictories. Likewise, a partner is not impossible in itself; what is impossible is its existence as a partner to the Creator. These two cases therefore resemble the impossibility of oddness in four: they arise from the relation expressed in a compound existential proposition. Yet the authors agree in using them to exemplify a simple existential proposition.

records.arabic: والجواب أن الامتناع لاجتماع النقيضين قد يعتبر بحيث يكون معقولا من الوجود المأخوذ رابطة بين الاجتماع والنقيضين كأن يقال هل للاجتماع وجود للنقيضين فحينئذ يكون مستفادا من الهلية المركبة وقد يعتبر بحيث يكون معقولا من الوجود المأخوذ محمولا كأن يقال هل اجتماع النقيضين موجود فيكون مستفادا من الهلية البسيطة وهذا هو المراد عند التمثيل ومورد محل حديث امتناع شريك الباري وغيره فتدبر فإنه دقيق ومزيد أيضا (قوله وإلا) أي فإن لم تكن ضرورة الوجود واللاوجود البسيطين أو المركبين بالنظر إلى ذات
records.english: The answer is that the impossibility of the conjunction of contradictories may be considered as understood from existence taken as a copula between conjunction and the contradictories: as though one asked, “Does conjunction exist for the two contradictories?” It would then be obtained from a compound existential proposition. Alternatively, it may be considered as understood from existence taken as the predicate: as though one asked, “Does the conjunction of contradictories exist?” It would then be obtained from a simple existential proposition. The latter is what is intended when giving the example, and is the setting in which the impossibility of a partner to the Creator and similar cases is discussed. Reflect: it is subtle, and [the final evaluative expression is uncertain]. On “Otherwise”: that is, if the necessity of existence and nonexistence, whether simple or compound, is not considered in relation to the essence of—

records.arabic: (أو لا ضرورتهما) للإمكان (لفظي) يقصد به تفسير مدلول اللفظ وضرورة التصور أي المغني عن التعريف المعنوي (وينقسم كل من الأولين) يعني الوجوب والامتناع دون الأخير أعني الإمكان لأنه ذاتي ليس إلا وإلا لكان الشيء واجبا أو ممتنعا أي ضروري الوجود أو العدم بالذات ولا ضروري الوجود والعدم بالغير فيرتفع ما بالذات وهذا معنى الانقلاب (إلى الذاتي والغيري) لأن ضرورة وجود الشيء أو لا وجوده في نفسه أو ضرورة وجوده لشيء أو لا وجوده له إن كانت بالنظر إلى ذات الموضوع كوجود الباري وعدم اجتماع النقيضين ووجود الزوجية للأربعة وعدم الفردية لها فذاتي وإلا فغيري (فالموصوف بالذاتي من
records.english: “Or the non-necessity of both,” as a definition of possibility, is “verbal”: its purpose is to explain what the expression signifies. The necessity of the conception means that it dispenses with a definition of the meaning. “Each of the first two”—necessity and impossibility, but not the last, namely possibility, since possibility is intrinsic only—“is divided into intrinsic and extrinsic.” Otherwise, a thing could be necessary or impossible, that is, necessarily existent or nonexistent intrinsically, yet neither necessarily existent nor necessarily nonexistent through another. What belongs to it intrinsically would then be removed: this is what a reversal [of its intrinsic modal status] means. The necessity of a thing’s existence or nonexistence in itself, or of its existence or nonexistence for something, is intrinsic when considered in relation to the subject’s own essence. Examples are the Creator’s existence, the non-occurrence of the conjunction of contradictories, the presence of evenness in four, and the absence of oddness from four. Otherwise it is extrinsic. “Thus that which is qualified as intrinsic among—”
